venue.name: Christ Church Cathedral
venue.description: Christ Church Cathedral is the Anglican cathedral of the Diocese of British Columbia at 930 Burdett Avenue in Victoria, built in thirteenth-century Gothic style to a 1896 competition design by J.C.M. Keith and completed in stages between 1929 and 1991. It is one of Canada's largest churches, with interior dimensions of 93 by 140 feet and towers 122 feet above street level, and its doors are open daily for worship, prayer, meditation or just to visit. A seven-circuit labyrinth on the south lawn is open to everyone to walk. The cathedral's own Facility Use Policy states that formal tours are offered regularly and can be booked through the Parish Administrator, and that rooms and grounds may be rented by external groups for a fee.

facility_notes.bus_parking: Limited on-site parking may be available, but normally cannot be guaranteed. Street parking is available on Quadra Street, Burdett Avenue, and Rockland Avenue, as well as at the south entrance to the Cathedral off Burdett.
facility_notes.lunch_space: A Chapter Room with kitchen (space for approximately 60 people lecture style) and the Chapel of the New Jerusalem with half-kitchen (seating up to 100) can be rented; external groups are required to provide their own coffee, tea, other beverages, food, and table cloths.

restrictions: All minor children must be supervised by a parent or guardian, or a person authorized by the parent or guardian at all times. (Facility Use Policy, external group rentals)
Neither smoking nor the use of recreational drugs is permitted on Cathedral property.

The cathedral nave and chapels are normally kept available for quiet personal prayer and meditation. Any other uses must be approved by the Parish Administrator and must be in keeping with the sacred nature of the space.

Individuals and groups wishing to use any cathedral space, indoors or out, for photographs must contact the Parish Administrator. The exception to this is visitors who wish to view the cathedral and to take a small number of personal photos, including selfies.
External groups renting the facilities must carry liability insurance of at least $5 million and pay a $100 refundable security/damage deposit.

programs.name: Formal cathedral tour
programs.description: The cathedral's Facility Use Policy (revised April 2024, posted March 2025) states that formal tours of the cathedral are offered regularly and may be booked through the Parish Administrator or online, and that private tours must be arranged through the Parish Administrator. No price, duration, group size, age range or schedule for the tours is published on the public site. The 'Discover the Cathedral' programme page (/programs/discover-the-cathedral) redirects to a login screen, so any tour times or fees held there could not be read.
programs.our_note: The only current, on-site evidence that tours still run is a line in the facility rental policy — the programme page behind it is now members-only, so phone the office and confirm the tour is still offered before you plan a trip around it. Ask on the same call whether a tour can be shortened for young children; nothing on the site suggests one written for them.
programs.practical_summary: Tours are booked through the Parish Administrator by phone or email. Price, length, group size, age suitability, washrooms and lunch space are all unpublished, so this needs a call before it is bookable.
programs.evidence: Formal tours of the cathedral are offered regularly, and may be booked through the Parish Administrator, or on-line.

programs.name: Self-guided visit
programs.description: The cathedral is open to visitors outside service times and its doors are open daily for worship, prayer, meditation, or just to visit. Published visiting hours differ between pages (see conflicts). No admission charge, donation expectation, group rate or group booking process for a self-guided visit is stated anywhere on the site.
programs.what_children_do: Walk into a very large stone church — the nave is 93 by 140 feet with towers 122 feet above the street — and look at the windows, the organ, the baptistry and the bells from the floor, quietly, since the nave and chapels are kept for personal prayer and meditation.
programs.our_note: It is a working church rather than a museum, so the visit is looking and keeping quiet — short and calm suits it, and a noisy group will land badly. Nothing on the site tells you whether a group of children needs to give notice, so ring the office at 250.383.2714 first rather than arriving with twenty of them.
programs.practical_summary: Free entry is not stated either way, and washrooms, an indoor lunch space and step-free access are not mentioned anywhere on the site. The two published versions of the visiting hours disagree, so confirm the day you plan to come.
programs.evidence: The Cathedral is open to visitors from 8.30am - 5.30pm on weekdays.

programs.name: Labyrinth walk
programs.description: A permanent seven-circuit labyrinth on the south lawn, created by the Mission and Outreach Team as a Millennium Project and open to everyone to walk. The seven-circuit design was chosen to provide easier access for wheelchairs and walkers and to give more space for all walkers. It is a single unbroken path in and out rather than a maze. No booking, fee, opening hours or group process is stated.
programs.what_children_do: Follow one unbroken path on the lawn at whatever pace suits, in to the centre and back out again, alone or beside someone else, stepping aside to pass anyone coming the other way.
programs.our_note: This is the part of the site that actually works for a small, young group: outdoors, no ropes to hold, no door to be quiet behind, and nothing to book. It is on an open city lawn with no fence mentioned, so plan your adult positions accordingly, and the cathedral's own framing of it is meditative rather than a game.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors on the south lawn, step-free enough that the design was chosen for wheelchairs and walkers, and nothing needs booking. There is no rain cover, no stated washroom and no lunch space.
programs.evidence: The seven circuit labyrinth is located on the south lawn and is available for everyone to walk.
